name: Evidence ancestry is defined and one artifact-to-invocation edge class is implemented; the graph is not composable
notes: Found on 2026-08-14 while assessing whether C3's ancestry dependency was as close to reachable as its equivalence dependency had turned out to be. It is not, and the asymmetry is instructive. Equivalence was one pure function because Slice B had already built the representation AND populated the evidence. Ancestry has representation fragments, no governed relation, and empty values in the fields that exist.

Section 4.15 states the ceiling and it should not be exceeded: one artifact may mix original observation, copied finding, new inference and paraphrase, so artifact-level lineage cannot distinguish them, and what the system can provide is artifact-level potential-dependence detection rather than claim-level independence proof. A first slice that attempted claim-level derivation would overclaim against the admitted ontology's own statement.

Six enforcement-matrix rows name ancestry or lineage in their dependency column: C3 per-kind equivalence check plus lineage traversal, C4 context-lineage inspection, C5 categorical assessment with reasons, C9 inheritance propagation, C10 VerificationRun with verifier-ancestry check, and C11 admission validator requiring disclosure and named controls. This is the single largest shared dependency among the six manual-mode constraints.

Recorded as its own gap rather than folded into GAP-0005 on the reviewing executor's recommendation. GAP-0005 is about invocation authorization having no record form and about six constraints claiming manual enforcement without artifacts; this is a distinct deficiency in what a constraint's central term means, and burying it would repeat the pattern where a gap's evidence describes several unrelated things and goes stale as a whole.

RECONCILED 2026-08-17 after PLAN-20260817-0001 completed. The reviewing executor found that this gap still described the pre-v9.2 world: evidence ancestry undefined, 210 records with no reference, and a five-step first slice beginning with a definition. The definition is admitted, the slice is complete, and two authenticated references exist.

The structural point is worth recording beyond this gap. The self-model audit reported ok true and verified_current throughout, because that audit establishes index-to-repository consistency and does not establish that a gap's narrative evidence remains semantically current. This is the second time a gap's evidence went stale while the audit stayed green; GAP-0005 was reconciled for the same reason on 2026-08-12. Nothing in the repository detects it.
recommended_first_slice: Not generalised traversal. A traversal over one edge class is architecturally uninteresting: with only artifact-to-invocation edges there is no chain to walk. The next slice should add a second directional edge class that COMPOSES with the first. Two candidates are named by Section 4.19 and by the completed plan: an invocation-to-artifact produced_by relation, and content-addressed output-to-effective-input linkage. produced_by is the more promising because it composes immediately: invocation A produced_by artifact A, artifact A effective input of invocation B, therefore invocation A is an ancestor of invocation B under Section 4.19's transitive closure, which is the relation C3 asks about. MEASURE BEFORE CHOOSING, as was done for C7 and for this gap's own first slice, where the packaging executor's cost estimates were wrong twice. The measurement is: of the 139 comparison artifacts, how many can already be unambiguously attributed to the InvocationRecords that produced them, and what retained evidence establishes that attribution? If attribution is nearly represented, produced_by is the cheaper slice. If it is not, output digesting may be the cleaner primitive. Build neither until the measurement says which.
risk: C3 remains unevaluable for any real claim, and the shape of the remaining gap is easy to mistake for progress. Its equivalence half resolves and blocks for every live pair under DECISION-20260814-0001. Its ancestry half now returns coverage complete for two invocations, which reads like success but establishes only that a named artifact reached those executors. C3 asks whether an equivalent executor appears in a claim's evidence ancestry; with no invocation-to-invocation edge, no executor can appear in any ancestry, so the constraint cannot be evaluated however many artifact edges accumulate. The specific hazard is that a future implementation composes what exists, finds no executor conflict because none is representable, and reports independence. C14 forbids reading a negative traversal as independence, and ancestry_edges reports coverage alongside edges for that reason, but the guard is one function's discipline rather than a property of the graph.
summary: ABS-0004 v9.2 Section 4.19 defines artifact-level evidence ancestry and C12 to C14 are admitted. PLAN-20260817-0001 implemented and verified the first edge class: an artifact selected into a retained ContextManifest and rendered into a captured invocation's effective input is a direct ancestor of that invocation. Two InvocationRecords carry an authenticated content-addressed reference and evaluate to coverage complete. What remains is that the graph has one edge class and no composition. All edges run artifact to invocation, so no invocation is an ancestor of any other, which is the relation C3 actually asks about. Neither of the other representations Section 4.19 names is implemented: content-addressed output-to-effective-input linkage needs output digests that do not exist, and an invocation-to-artifact produced_by edge class is covered by no admitted plan.
